author: human
request:
Feature request: filter the vet list by specialty. Three product decisions
come with it, made here as the product owner:

- Non-goal NG-9 is narrowed: free-text veterinarian search stays out of
  scope, but filtering the directory by an attribute it already shows is in.
  Record the narrowing the way the project records non-goal changes.
- The JSON endpoint at /vets is reinstated as a supported surface — this
  filter is its first requested capability. Mint a fresh requirement for it;
  the withdrawn REQ-VET-002 stays withdrawn and its id is not reused.
- The filter is a URL contract only. Neither surface gains a form, dropdown,
  or other page control in this request; pagination links carry the
  parameter so filtered pages stay navigable. A visible control may come as
  a follow-up request.

Both vet list surfaces accept an optional `specialty` query parameter:

- /vets.html?specialty=<name> — the HTML page shows only vets holding that
  specialty; pagination applies to the filtered list.
- /vets?specialty=<name> — the JSON endpoint returns only those vets.

Matching is on the whole specialty name, case-insensitive — not a prefix. A
specialty matching no vet yields the normal page or JSON document with an
empty vet list (HTTP 200). An empty or whitespace-only value behaves as if
the parameter were absent, like the empty owner search. Without the parameter
both endpoints behave as today. Cover the new behavior with tests.

These are all the product decisions; no further product answer will come
during the work. Where a choice still seems open, take the narrowest reading
consistent with this request and record the open question rather than
waiting.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Veterinarian directory narrows to one specialty on both surfaces
summary: Both veterinarian directory surfaces, the reader page and the machine-readable list, accept an optional specialty in the request address and show only veterinarians holding it. Matching is on the whole name, ignoring letter case. A blank value lists everyone; no value keeps today's behavior. Recorded in the PRD as REQ-VET-003.
acceptance_criteria: GET /vets.html?specialty=radiology renders the vet list page carrying only veterinarians who hold radiology, with every other element of the page unchanged
GET /vets?specialty=radiology returns a JSON document whose vet list carries only veterinarians who hold radiology
matching ignores letter case on both surfaces: specialty=RADIOLOGY and specialty=radiology select the same veterinarians
matching is on the whole specialty name, not a prefix: specialty=radio selects no veterinarian on either surface
a specialty no veterinarian holds returns HTTP 200 with the normal page or JSON document and an empty vet list, on both surfaces
an empty or whitespace-only specialty value behaves as if the parameter were absent and lists every veterinarian, mirroring the empty owner search of REQ-OWN-002
with no specialty parameter present, both surfaces behave exactly as they do today
pagination applies to the filtered HTML list: page size and page count are computed over the filtered veterinarians
every paging link on a filtered vet list page carries the same specialty, so following one keeps the list filtered
neither surface gains a form, dropdown, or other page control for choosing the specialty in this slice
non_goals: a form, dropdown, or any other page control for choosing the specialty
free-text search of veterinarians by name
narrowing either surface by any attribute other than specialty
searching for a pet or a visit
notes: PRD requirement id for this capability is REQ-VET-003 in the Veterinarian directory section; this record's req_id is the intake slice id. REQ-VET-002 stays withdrawn and its id is not reused; the Superseded list now records that the machine-readable surface it described is reinstated under REQ-VET-003. docs/adr/README.md needs an index row for adr/2026-08-15-non-goal-veterinarian-search-narrowing.md; that file is outside this agent's write scope. Three open questions recorded in the PRD rather than consulted: a visible specialty control, further capabilities of the machine-readable list, and whether the NG-9 narrowing reaches past specialty.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: The narrowing reuses the owner-search shape already in the codebase: an optional request parameter normalized in the controller, a derived Spring Data finder carrying the match, and Spring's Page carrying the paging. What is new, and now recorded in adr/2026-08-15-specialty-narrowing-in-the-vet-query.md, is where the match lives and whether it is cached. The match lives in the repository query, because architecture-principles.md § Pattern Catalog admits no new business rule in a controller, and because expressing case-insensitivity in the query avoids repeating the per-vendor divergence recorded for REQ-OWN-002 under system-design.md § Known Defects. The narrowed finder carries no cache annotation: the vets cache declares no size limit and no eviction, so keying it on caller-supplied text would let any client grow it without bound. Both surfaces call the one finder, the machine-readable one unpaged, so they cannot drift apart on matching. Basis: the covering symbols were resolved by reading VetController, VetRepository, Vet, CacheConfiguration, OwnerController, OwnerRepository, and vetList.html directly; the IDE oracle is not connected in this dispatch, so this is the weaker file-read basis rather than a symbol lookup.
integration_points: VetRepository gains one finder selecting veterinarians by specialty name, case-insensitively, returning a Page and carrying no cache annotation
/vets.html binds an optional specialty parameter, normalizes blank to absent, and puts the normalized value in the model for the paging links
/vets calls the same finder with an unpaged request when a specialty is given, and keeps today's cached findAll when none is
no change to Vet, Specialty, the Vets wrapper shape, the schema, or the seed data
no new route and no new page control; both existing routes gain one optional parameter

risks.risk: Derived property-path resolution: Vet maps a Set field but exposes getSpecialties returning a List, so the plain derived name may not resolve.
risks.mitigation: Use the explicit underscore form for the nested path; an explicitly parameterized JPQL query is the sanctioned fallback under security-principles.md § Realization. Concatenated query text is not.

risks.risk: The eager many-to-many association could be reused by the predicate join, truncating each returned veterinarian's specialty list to the matched one.
risks.mitigation: Assert that a veterinarian holding more than one specialty still shows all of them on a narrowed listing, per the acceptance criterion that every other element of the page is unchanged.

risks.risk: Composing the paging links by string concatenation would place request-derived text directly into an href.
risks.mitigation: Use Thymeleaf's parameterized link expression form, which encodes the parameter value, rather than concatenating it into the URL string.

risks.risk: Emitting an empty specialty parameter into the links of an unnarrowed page would change today's rendered output.
risks.mitigation: Keep the unnarrowed page's paging links exactly as they are today; verify what the template engine emits for an absent value rather than assuming it is omitted.

risks.risk: A later change adding a cache annotation to the narrowed finder would key an unbounded cache on caller-supplied text.
risks.mitigation: The omission and its reason are recorded in adr/2026-08-15-specialty-narrowing-in-the-vet-query.md, so the annotation cannot be restored as an oversight fix.

author: code-quality-reviewer
recommendations: VetController.narrowingSpecialty() returns null to mean "no narrowing", and the null then travels through findVets/findVetList (VetController.java:87-104) and into the Thymeleaf model/template (${specialty == null} in vetList.html) as the sentinel. The checklist calls for Optional over null for nullable returns; OwnerController's analogous pattern (OwnerController.java:97-102, the pattern this design explicitly mirrors) avoids the sentinel entirely by normalizing to "" and always calling the same finder, which the specialty case can't do because findBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase is an equals-match with no empty-string "match everything" behavior - so the null branch here is defensible, but wrapping the private helper's return in Optional<String> (unwrapped once at the Model.addAttribute call) would keep the null out of the two branching helpers and read closer to the project's own convention.

Javadoc consistency: narrowingSpecialty() (VetController.java:80-89) carries full @param/@return tags; the block comment on findVetList() (VetController.java:96-101) reads as Javadoc but has no @return, and findVets() has no comment at all. Not blocking, but the three private helpers introduced together would read more uniformly with the same documentation shape.

vetList.html's five paging-link sites (lines 37, 42, 47, 52, 57) each state the link address twice via a ${specialty == null} ? ... : ... ternary, producing ten near-identical addresses to keep in step and lines over 140 characters. This is a knowingly accepted, documented tradeoff (adr/2026-08-15-specialty-narrowing-in-the-vet-query.md and the design-block's risks list already name it and defer extraction as a follow-up), so it is not a fresh finding - flagging only so the deferred refactor stays visible to the next reader of this template.
approved_aspects: Naming follows architecture-principles.md § Naming - no prohibited suffixes, VetRepository's new finder follows Spring Data derivation conventions, and method names read as verbs without repeating the type name
The repository finder's omission of @Cacheable is explained in both the Javadoc and the ADR, closing off the unbounded-cache risk the design-block flagged rather than leaving it implicit

Case-insensitive, whole-name matching is expressed once in the repository query (findBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase) and both surfaces call it, so the HTML and JSON paths cannot drift apart on what matches
The paging-link encoding uses the parameterized @{...(...)} Thymeleaf form throughout, so request-derived text never reaches an href via string concatenation
checkFormat and checkstyleMain both pass clean on the diff; no formatting or style-check regressions

Consulted OwnerController.java:94-119 directly (grep/read basis - no IDE oracle was connected for this dispatch, per the build-pass disclosure) to check the null-sentinel choice against the codebase's existing optional-narrowing-parameter pattern

author: test-reviewer

findings.description: VetController.narrowingSpecialty strips surrounding whitespace from a non-blank specialty value (Javadoc: 'Surrounding blanks are stripped so they do not defeat the whole-name match'), and the design-block notes confirm this is a recorded behavior. Every existing non-blank test value ('radiology', 'RADIOLOGY', 'radio', 'cardiology', 'surgery') has no surrounding whitespace, so the strip() call is line-covered (100% per jacoco) but its actual trimming effect is never behaviorally exercised - a regression that stopped stripping (e.g. an accidental .trim() vs .strip() swap or a removed call) would not fail any test. The blank-only test ('   ') takes the other branch of the ternary and never reaches strip() at all.
findings.fix: Add a case (web-layer or ClinicServiceTests) asserting a specialty value with surrounding whitespace around real text, e.g. specialty=" radiology ", still matches the vets holding radiology - matching the acceptance criterion's normalization behavior with an actual assertion, not just line coverage.

findings.description: The design-block records a risk explicitly: composing paging links by string concatenation would place request-derived text directly into an href, mitigated by switching all five paging-link sites to the parameterized @{/vets.html(...)} Thymeleaf form, which URL-encodes the specialty value. No test exercises a specialty value containing characters that require URL/HTML encoding (e.g. an ampersand, a space-substitute, or a reserved URI character) to confirm the encoding actually happens on a rendered link. The current tests only use alphabetic specialty values ('radiology', 'surgery', 'cardiology'), so the mitigation for this named risk is asserted by design reasoning only, never by an executable test.
findings.fix: Add a paging-link test using a specialty value containing a character requiring encoding (e.g. "large animal" with a space, or a value containing '&') and assert the rendered href carries the correctly percent-encoded parameter rather than a raw, unescaped one.

approved_aspects: The web-layer VetControllerTests correctly limits itself to controller wiring (parameter normalization, dispatch to the right repository method, view/model shape) while the real match semantics - whole-name, case-insensitive, multi-vendor-safe comparison expressed via upper() in the derived query - are independently verified against a real database in ClinicServiceTests.shouldFindVetsHoldingASpecialtyIgnoringLetterCase and shouldNotMatchVetsOnPartOfASpecialtyName. A wrong repository method name or wrong query semantics would fail at least one of these two layers, so the repository stub in the web test cannot mask a broken query.

The eager many-to-many truncation risk named in the design-block is genuinely covered: ClinicServiceTests.shouldStillCarryEverySpecialtyOfAVetMatchedOnOneOfThem runs against the real database and asserts a multi-specialty vet keeps every specialty after being matched on only one of them.

The byte-identical unfiltered-paging-links risk is well covered: theVetListPageShouldListEveryVetWhenNoSpecialtyIsGiven asserts both the exact unfiltered href text and the absence of any 'specialty=' anywhere on the page. theVetListPagingLinksShouldCarryTheSpecialty, read across its two requests (page=1 and page=2), exercises all five doubled paging-link sites (first, previous, next, last, and both numbered-link branches) via the positive containsString and negative not(containsString(...\")) assertion pair, so a single broken site among the five would be caught.

All 12 PRD-named test names are present and map onto the 10 acceptance criteria; the suite adds one extra web-layer test (theVetListPageShouldStillShowEverySpecialtyOfAListedVet) as further belt-and-braces coverage of the truncation risk.
Four-phase structure, BDD test naming, and factory-method construction (radiology(), surgery(), sixRadiologists()) are followed consistently with the host file's existing idiom.

author: security-reviewer
recommendations: Supply chain NOT VERIFIED against the NVD in this review. build.gradle declares no OWASP dependency-check plugin (plugins are java, checkstyle, jacoco, spring-boot 4.1.0, dependency-management 1.1.7, graalvm native 1.1.2, cyclonedx 3.2.4, javaformat 0.0.47), so dependencyCheckAnalyze could not run and this reviewer has no network access. The change adds no dependency and does not touch build.gradle, so the slice itself introduces no supply-chain delta - but the resolved Spring Boot 4.1.0 / Jackson tree remains unchecked against the NVD. A human or CI should close this check; consider wiring dependencyCheckAnalyze into the gate.

Low-severity availability note, no fix requested: before this change /vets was served entirely from the vets cache, so no caller could force a database round trip on that route. With ?specialty=<anything> both vet routes now issue an uncached query per request. The tradeoff is deliberate and correct (the alternative was unbounded cache growth), the query is a bounded equality match, and an equivalent uncached caller-parameterized query already exists on the open /owners search - so this is not weaker than the recorded baseline. Worth remembering if rate limiting or a bounded cache is ever added.

Pre-existing, outside this diff: ownersList.html still builds paging hrefs with __${...}__ preprocessing (lines 22, 44, 49, 54) and @{'/owners?page=' + ${i}} concatenation (line 35). The values interpolated today are integers and entity ids, so there is no current exploit, but the pattern evaluates its result as a template expression and is one request-derived value away from being one. The form this slice adopted for vetList.html is the safe replacement; migrating ownersList.html would retire the pattern from the codebase.

Static-analysis scope, per the build-pass disclosure: no IntelliJ inspection ran on this diff and the IDE oracle was not connected in this dispatch either, so every claim above rests on reading the diff and the working-tree files plus grep - the weaker basis rather than symbol resolution. No access-control or route-exposure claim in this review turns on symbol resolution (the change adds no route and no security configuration), so the missing oracle does not leave a claim unsupported here.
approved_aspects: Injection into data access: the caller-supplied specialty reaches the database only through the derived finder VetRepository.findBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase(String, Pageable). No string-concatenated or interpolated query text is introduced anywhere in the diff; the value stays a bound parameter. Matches the SQL-injection mitigation recorded in system-design.md Threat Model.

Cross-site scripting: the request-derived specialty is written into the model and rendered only inside th:href link expressions with a fixed literal path, @{/vets.html(page=...,specialty=${specialty})}. Thymeleaf URL-encodes the query-parameter value and HTML-escapes the attribute, and the base path is a literal so no javascript:/data: URI can be injected. Default output escaping is not disabled anywhere in the diff; no th:utext and no DOM injection is added.

Template-expression injection: the change removes the pre-existing __${...}__ preprocessing from all five paging links in vetList.html and replaces it with link expressions. Request-derived text never enters a preprocessed expression. This is a net reduction in the template's expression-evaluation surface, not merely a neutral change.

Cache poisoning / unbounded cache growth: findBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase deliberately carries no @Cacheable, so caller-supplied text cannot key the size-unlimited, eviction-free vets cache. The Javadoc states the reason and cites the ADR; this is the correct call under least privilege and is verified against CacheConfiguration.

No new attack surface: no new route, no new dependency (build.gradle unchanged), no form or binder added, no file, path, process, network, serialization, reflection, logging, or credential handling touched. Grep of src/main/java/.../vet/ for Runtime./ProcessBuilder/enableDefaultTyping/JsonTypeInfo/System.out//tmp/ returns nothing. No secret-shaped literal appears in the diff.

Response-size bound: the /vets JSON surface calls the narrowed finder with Pageable.unpaged(), which returns at most the same rows the pre-existing unpaged findAll() already returned. The narrowing can only shrink the response, never grow it, so no new unbounded-allocation path is added.

Pattern consistency justified: vetList.html's paging links now diverge from ownersList.html's preprocessing style. The divergence is justified inline in a parser-level comment and moves to the safer of the two forms, satisfying the Pattern Consistency clause.

blast_radius.note: Three production files in one package: the vet controller, one added repository finder, and the vet list template. Both HTTP surfaces change only by gaining an optional parameter, so an unnarrowed request on either is routed to the exact cached finder it used before; the widest hunk group is the five paging links in vetList.html, all confined to that one page.

semantic_surprise.note: Read every hunk: narrowingSpecialty is hasText ? strip() : null with no inverted condition, findVets and findVetList both branch on null to the cached whole-list finders, and all five template ternaries map the null branch to the parameterless address and the non-null branch to the same page number plus the specialty, with no off-by-one against the originals they replace. The one asymmetry a reader might not expect, that the narrowed finder is uncached while both whole-list finders stay Cacheable, is pre-declared in the query ADR and in the repository Javadoc.

test_adequacy.note: The controller tests are real, not tautological, asserting rendered content, model attributes, encoded hrefs and negative cases across fifteen scenarios. But the narrowed finder is only exercised against a live database with Pageable.unpaged(); every paged assertion runs against a hand-written stub in VetControllerTests that reimplements paging in Java. The requirement's own done-when clause, that a narrowed listing pages, is therefore pinned nowhere against a database, and a derived query that paged wrongly over the specialties join with Vet's eager collection would leave the whole suite green.
